newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unemployment rose in Oct - trade union group.
newsitem.headline: German unemployment rose in Oct - trade union group.

text.p: German unemployment is likely to have risen slightly in October, the DGB trade union federation said late on Wednesday.

Joblessness in western Germany is likely to have risen by 15,000-20,000, a bigger increase than the 3,700 rise in October last year, the DGB said. In east Germany, unemployment may have fallen slightly, the DGB said.
The DGB also said that seasonally-adjusted unemployment probably increased in western as well as eastern Germany.
The Federal Labour Office is due to publish October jobless figures at 0855 GMT on Thursday.

In September, the unadjusted pan-German jobless total fell to 3.848 million from 3.902 million. On a seasonally-adjusted basis, joblessness rose 39,000 to 3.991 million. The adjusted unemployment rate rose to 10.4 percent from 10.3 percent.
The adjusted figures also marked a rise from October 1995, when 3.663 million were unemployed in Germany, 2.559 in the western region of the country and 1.076 in the former East Germany.
In western Germany, the unadjusted unemployment rate for October rose to 9.0 percent, up from 8.9 percent in September and 7.9 percent in October 1995.
Eastern German's October rate equalled the 14.7 percent reported last month. In October 1995, the figure was 13.0 percent.

Along with the new unemployment totals, the Labour Office said the number of workers on short time increased to 231,319 in October, up 30,133 from the previous month. The number of short-time workers in western Germany rose 29,960 to 182,573. In eastern Germany the figure increased by 173 to 48,746, the Labour Office said.
